en: (Kṛti No. 144) (Pariśiṣṭa No. 1322) (Title: Parāmbārcanacandrikā)

(Leaf 74, Tantra Complete) || Salutations to Śrī Gaṇeśa. Salutations to the venerable Guru and the goddess Parāmbā. I bow to the pair of feet of the venerable Gurunātha, the Lord of the hosts of gods, the bestower of knowledge, and the all-pervading one.

I shall now perform a very concise worship according to the sequence of Śrīvidyā, dedicated to the venerable Śāradāmbā, whose face is like the moon of autumn; this is intended as an authoritative guide for virtuous, diligent, and learned devotees whose souls are endowed with true devotion. Herein, first is the extraction of the Vidyā, as stated in the Tantrarāja:

I am proclaimed by the playful movements of the heart, the vital breath (prāṇa), the *ilā* wind, the *haṃsa*, the fire, and the individual soul (*sva*). Listen as I describe these three types according to their distinctions in due order:
the first is situated at the beginning of *haṃsa*; the second is situated between *dā* and *haṃsa*; and that very third is the *prakṛti* situated at the end of the fourth.
"Through *māyā*, there shall be liberation by means of the fourth [turiya]; and through the other three, there shall be prosperity.

Thus have the *vidyās* of Tripurasundarī been correctly proclaimed. The letter *ha* is the heart; the letter *ka* is the vital breath (*prāṇa*); the letter *la* is the earth (*ilā*). These are the three syllables of the *haṃsa*.
The letter *kā* (ka) is joined with the burning *repha* (*ra*). *Vahni* is the letter *ī*; it is joined with that. *Svaṃ* is the *anusvāra*;

by that, the seed-syllable of *māyā* is formed. By this, the collection of the *śakti-kūṭa* is produced. [She] whose beginning is *haṃsa* and so forth—*haṃsa* being that which begins with the letter *ha*—is at the beginning of the *śakti-kūṭa*. *Ha*...

By adding the letter *ha* to the *Vāgbhava* born from *kāra*, the *Kāmarāja-kūṭa* arises through the conjunction of the letter *ha* between the letters *ka* and *la*— which are situated at the beginning, middle, and end of the *Haṃsa-yātra-śakti-kūṭa*— by joining the letter *ha* in the middle of those two. Thus, *tā*.

The extraction of the third [syllable] consisting of the Vāgbhava and Kāmarāja kūṭas has been performed according to the sequence of dissolution, emission, and maintenance. Now, it may be asked: why were the Vāgbhava and Kāmarāja not extracted according to the order of the mantra—first extracting the third, and afterwards the Vāgbhava and Kāmarāja? It is said: [it is] by way of emission (*sṛṣṭi*).
The sequence ending in emission pertains to celibates; the sequence ending in withdrawal pertains to ascetics;

the sequence ending in maintenance pertains to householders, because maintenance exists between emission and withdrawal. [This sequence ending in maintenance] is for the purpose of all [practitioners'] entitlement to recitation (japa).

It has been previously extracted because it is the cause of liberation. Through the final *māyā* among all the *varṇas* brought forth by the *māyā* of the fourth state (*turya*), she becomes embodied in thirteen syllables; this is the meaning.
And so it has been stated by us in the *Saundaryalaharī*: "Śiva, Śakti, Kāma, Kṣi..."
The sun, the moon, the god of love, Indra, his followers, and the lions— these,
joined at their ends by three lines within the heart,
assume the nature of the limbs of the name of Janani (the Mother). Thus [ends the section on] the science of *itihā* and so forth.

The extraction of the *Atharva-vidyā*: In the *Śrī-Atharvaṇa-Rahasya* it is said: "Kāma, Yoni, Kamalā, Vajrapāṇi, Guhā, Hasa, Mātariśvan, Śramin, Indra, Punar, Guhā, Sakalā, and Māyā—this is the primordial *Vidyā*, the Mother of the Universe, consisting of many syllables."

And thus it has been said by us in the *Saurialaharī*: "Placing this triad— Smara, Yoni, and Lakṣmī— at the beginning of Your mantra, those who delight in the flavor of infinite great enjoyment constantly mutter You with a rosary of beads strung upon the thread of the *Cintāmaṇi*."
"Those who offer oblations of hundreds of streams of fragrant ghee into the auspicious fire."

Now, the sequence: there, the illustrious lord of practitioners, having risen at the end of the night, having performed the necessary rites, having discarded his night-garment and put on another garment, seated upon a comfortable seat and meditating on the Guru at his head, should perform the salutation to the Guru’s sandals. Dhyā...

One should meditate upon the Guru, who is seated upon a lion-throne situated in the center of the pericarp of the lotus of Brahmā; whose divine form is established there, who shines with the luster of moonstone, and who holds a rosary, a book, and the gestures of granting fearlessness and boons. He is clad in white garments, adorned with white unguents and flowers, and decorated with pearls and a joyful smile.

That two-eyed one, seated upon the lap of his left side with his red Shakti, possessing a gentle smile and being a treasury of intense compassion; [seated] upon a thousand-petaled lotus, shining with the luster of the full moon,
his lotus-hands granting boons and fearlessness, clad in pure fragrant flowers and garments, with a serene face and eyes.
One should remember the Guru, who has the form of the deity of the Kalā, seated upon a swan at the crown of the head, preceded by his name.

Having meditated thus, one should perform the prostration to the sandals (*pādukā-vaṃdana*). As follows: *Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hskhphreṃ hsauḥ hasakṣamalavarayūṃ sahakṣamalavarayīṃ amukāmbāsahitāmukānandanātha hsauḥ hskhphreṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ oṃ śrīgu*.

Having thus worshipped with these offerings, and considering one's own body to have been consecrated by the stream of nectar from His lotus feet, one should bow with the five mudrās: the *staṃbhanamudrā*, the *caturasramudrā*, the *matsyamudrā*, and the *gomukhamudrā*.

These are proclaimed as the five mudrās, renowned as the *yonimudrā*. One should daily praise [the Guru] with these five verses for the sake of attaining all perfections (*siddhis*). By reciting them at the time of awakening in the morning, the day shall become auspicious.

Having offered this, one should request permission for necessary duties. Oṃ.

O Supreme Lord, O Śrī Sundarī, consisting of universal consciousness, by the very command of your feet, having risen at dawn for the sake of your beloved, I shall carry on with the journey of worldly existence. 1.
O Supreme Goddess of the Triple City, by your command, I shall continue to follow the journey of saṃsāra.
O Mother, may rivalry, contempt, strife, negligence, and fear not overcome you.
I know what is dharma, yet I have no inclination toward it; I know what is adharma, yet I have no cessation from it.
O Great Goddess, I act exactly as I have been commanded by you, who abide within my heart. || 3 ||

Having worshipped one's own seat with "Lāsanāya namaḥ" and sitting upon a lotus-seat facing either east or north, one should then worship in the northeast direction with "Dīpanāthāya namaḥ," [saying]:
"In this field, for the sake of Dīpanātha as the cause of unimpeded success, [I worship] the Śrīcakra..."

Having requested, "Please grant me permission for the purpose of worship," and having received the command of Bhairava by saying, "O you with sharp fangs, great body, resembling the fire at the end of an aeon, salutations to you, O Bhairava; you should grant me permission," he worships upon the level ground with the mantra: *Oṃ devyāsanādhāraśaktaye namaḥ*.

One should draw the Triśrīcakra: the Bindu, the Triangle, the Eight-spoked [wheel], the inner and outer Ten-spoked [wheels], the Bhuvaneśvara [Eight-spoked wheel], then the Eight-petalled Lotus, the Kalā Lotus, and the enclosure of the Earth. Because of its existence; for in the *Vāmakeśvaratantra*, the *Jñānārṇava*, the *Dakṣiṇāmūrtisaṃhitā*, the *Subhagodaya*, the *Tripurātāpinī*, and other texts, it is stated that there is no separate circle drawn on the fourteen-petaled and eight-petaled lotuses, nor three concentric circles on the sixteen-petaled lotus. Thus...

Having fashioned a yantra for worship, or otherwise having prepared it with lines for the netherworld (pātāla), upward lines, the earth-plane (bhūprastha), or the Meru-plane (meruprastha), one should install it. One should arrange the offerings. One should place on the right side the articles for one's own worship.
On the left, one should set down a beautiful, well-adorned pitcher filled with highly fragrant water. One should place a vessel behind for the washing of the hands.
Then, on the northern part of the *cakra*, one should prepare a mandala consisting of a triangle, a circle, and a square.

Having formed the syllable *laṃ* (3), and having worshipped with the mantra *hrīṃ vyāpakamaṇḍalāyanaṃ*, one should place a vessel full of food and water upon the support (*ādhāra*) there; then, with all the fingers of the left hand, one should offer the oblation (*bali*) by pouring water while reciting: *oṃ hrīṃ sarvavighnakṛdbhyaḥ sarvabhūtebhyo huṃ svāhā*. One’s own...

Adorned with perfumes, garments, garlands, and ornaments, his body scented with camphor and musk, and with a joyful heart, meditating "I am indeed Brahman," he should prostrate, saying: "(3) Oṃ, obeisance to the Guru" on the left shoulder; "(3) Oṃ, to Gaṇapati" on the right shoulder; and "(3) Oṃ, to the Supreme Deity" at the heart. One should meditate upon the sandals of the Guru with the *saṃghaṭṭamudrā*. Then, having made the hands fragrant by rubbing scented substances with "AṂ ĀṂ SAUḤ," and having taken fragrant flowers with "HSRAIṂ," one should crush them and smell them with "OṂ HSRAUṂ TE SARVE."

Having recited, "May those who harm this [person] go to dissolution; may death, disease, fear, and afflictions fall upon the enemy," one should cast those flowers in the northern direction. Again, having purified the hands by rubbing them against each other with the *vidyā* for hand-purification (*karaśuddhi*), one should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of hand-purification. One should perform the placement (*nyāsa*) as follows: *thāṃ* on the two middle fingers; *āṃ* on the two ring fingers;

*sauḥ* on the two little fingers; *aṃ* on the two thumbs; *āṃ* on the two index fingers; and *sauḥ* on the palms and backs of the hands. Then, one should perform self-protection (*ātmarakṣā*): *aiṃ klīṃ sauḥ namas tripurasundari māṃ rakṣa*.

Having performed the pervasive placement (*vyāpaka-vinyāsa*) three times, reciting "rakṣa" (protect) from the head down to the feet, one should again recite [the mantra] and perform the binding of the ten directions with three claps of the hands— upward, into the intermediate space, and downward— and then, reciting it once more, one should contemplate a wall of fire by circling it three times around one's own head with sounds produced by the thumb and forefinger. Thus it is said.

Having performed self-protection (*ātmarakṣā*), one should perform the purification of the elements (*bhūtaśuddhi*). Then, having made the formal resolve (*saṃkalpa*)—"I shall perform the purification of the elements for the sake of attaining qualification"—one should raise the Kuṇḍalinī from the Mūlādhāra by means of the syllable *Huṃ*, unite it with the individual soul (*jīvātman*), and dissolve it into the Supreme Self (*paramātman*) with the sound *Hum*. Then, [from] the feet up to the knees...
One should dissolve the earth situated within the body into water; one should dissolve the water from the knees up to the navel into fire;
one should dissolve the fire from the navel up to the heart into air;

one should dissolve the air from the heart up to the space between the eyebrows into ether; [and one should dissolve that which is situated] from the space between the eyebrows up to the aperture of Brahmā (brahmarandhra) [into the supreme state].

One should dissolve the ego (ahaṃkāra) into space (ākāśa); the great principle (mahattattva) into primordial nature (prakṛti); and that primordial nature into Brahman. Then, one should contemplate the personification of sin (pāpapuruṣa) within the left side of the abdomen: having the murder of a Brahmin for its head, the theft of gold for its two arms, the drinking of liquor for its heart, and violating the teacher’s bed for its hips.

One should meditate upon that [wind] within the left side of the belly as having two parts, consisting of a pair of words associated with it; having limbs and minor limbs that are sins, with hair like secondary sins (upapātaka), red beard and eyes, holding a sword and shield, black in color, the size of a thumb, facing downwards, and possessing three eyes. Then, [one should meditate on] the wind-seed syllable *yaṃ*, which is smoke-colored and sixteen...

Repeating the syllable *raṃ* sixty-four times— this being the fire-seed (*vahnibīja*) of red color— one should fill the breath through both the left and right nostrils, dry up the body that is the form of sin, and by means of the practice of *kumbhaka* (breath retention) through the left and right nostrils, burn the sinful body to ashes. Then, [repeating] *yaṃ*, the wind...
Repeating the seed-syllable (*bīja*) thirty-two times, one should expel the ashes of the personified sin through the right nostril.

Then, by uttering *vaṃ*, one causes a rain of nectar consisting of the *mātṛkā* letters to fall from the moon on the forehead, drenching the ashes. Having formed the limbs [of the body] according to the sequence of ritual placement (*nyāsa*), one makes it firm by reciting *alaṃ* and [becomes] supreme.
From the Self comes its own nature (prakṛti); from that, the Great Principle (mahattattva); from that, the ego-sense (ahaṃkāra); from the ego-sense, space (ākāśa);

from space, air (vāyu); from air, fire (agni); from fire, water (āpaḥ); from water, earth (pṛthivī). Having thus established the elements in their proper places, one should draw the vital breath (prāṇa) into the heart with the mantra "I am That" (so'ham), and [enter] the wall...
One should place [the elements] in their respective positions and contemplate one's own self as transcending the phenomenal world;

this is the purification of the elements (*bhūtaśuddhi*). Then, placing the hand upon the heart, one recites: *Āṃ hrīṃ kroṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ hauṃ haṃsaḥ mama prāṇā iha sthitāḥ | mama jīva iha sthitaḥ | mama sarve...* (13) ...[my vital breaths are established here; my life-force is established here; all my...]

The application (*viniyoga*) for the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) as limbs of the Vidyā is as follows: *mā* to the goddess Sarasvatī at the mouth; *aṃ* to the seed-syllable (*bīja*) at the heart; *aḥ* to the power (*śakti*) at the private parts; *kṣaṃ* to the pin (*kīlaka*) at the navel.
*Aṃ kaṃ* (four times), *īṃ*, salutation (*namaḥ*) to the heart. *Iṃ caṃ* (four times), *īṃ*, *svāhā* to the head. *Uṃ ṭaṃ* (four times), *ūṃ* to the tuft of hair (*śikhā*).
*Khāyai vaṣaṭ; aiṃ kavacāya huṃ; oṃ paṃ auṃ netratrayāya vauṣaṭ;
aṃ yaṃ [raṃ laṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ l̥ kṣaṃ] aḥ astrāya phaṭ.* Having performed the pervasive application (*vyāpaka*) with these fifty-one *mātṛkā* letters, one should meditate.
As for the meditation: "She who resembles ten million moons released from their crescents... [āpī...]*

"I take refuge in the primordial Goddess Vāgīśvarī, who has breasts that are not too high, whose head is adorned with the crescent moon, whose three eyes are rolling from the intoxication of honey-wine, who constantly holds a rosary, a trident, and a skull-cup in her hands, who is proud of her youth, and whose body is smeared [with ashes]. Having thus meditated, one should perform the internal placement of the Mātṛkās (Antarmātṛkā-nyāsa).

For purification, one should place the sixteen vowels upon the sixteen petals of the *viśuddha* [cakra] as follows: starting from its own front petal, one should place them as *aṃ namaḥ*, *āṃ namaḥ*, *i* [namaḥ], and so forth. In the *anāhata* [cakra] with twelve petals, one should place the letters from *ka* to *ṭha*. In the *maṇipūra* [cakra] with ten petals, one should place the letters from *ḍa* to *pha*. In the *svādhiṣṭhāna* [cakra] with six petals, [one should place the letters] from *ba*...

One should place *lāṃ* and *tāṃ* [at the heart]. One should place the letters from *va* to *sa* on the four-petaled *ādhāra*. One should place *haṃ* and *kṣaṃ* on the two petals of the *ājñā* [cakra]. This is the internal *mātṛkā*. Then, one should place the pure (*śuddha*) *mātṛkā* on the outside.
He states the locations suitable for that: the forest, the circle, the two eyes, and the ears.

One should sequentially assign the syllables known as the "pervasive" (*vyāpaka*) to these locations: on the cheeks, lips, rows of teeth, head, and mouth; on the joints and tips of the arms and feet; on both sides, the back, the navel, and the abdomen; on the heart, the roots of the arms, the throat, and the armpits; on the heart and so forth, up to the pair of hands and feet; and on the abdomen and face. In these places...
One should perform the placement (*nyāsa*) of the fifty-one letters beginning with *A* and ending with *Kṣa*, including the *Bindu* and the *Mātṛkā*.

This is the *Śuddhamātṛkā-nyāsa*: *Aṃ* (with *namaḥ*) on the head; *Āṃ* (0) on the face-circle; *Iṃ* (0) on the right eye; *Īṃ* (0) on the left eye; *Uṃ* (0) on the right ear; *Ūṃ* (0) on the left ear; *Ṛṃ* (0) on the right nostril; *Ṝṃ* (0) on the left [nostril].

One should perform the pervasive placement (*vyāpaka-nyāsa*) with the letters *ḍā* and *ḍi* on the left hand and foot; *ḷaṃ* on the abdomen; and *kṣaṃ* on the mouth, using all the letters of the Mātṛkā.

Then follows the mantra-placement (*mantra-nyāsa*). Having performed three rounds of breath control (*prāṇāyāma*) with the root mantra, one should perform the placement of the seer (*ṛṣi*) and so forth as follows:
*Oṃ, of this great mantra of the venerable Goddess Lalitā Tripurasundarī...*

(3) *Aṃ śikhāyai vaṣaṭ* on the two middle fingers; (3) *Āṃ kavacāya huṃ* on the two ring fingers;

(3) *Hrīṃ Astrāya Phaṭ* to the palms and backs of the hands. This is the six-limbed (*ṣaḍaṅga*) ritual using the phonemes and the *Māyā-bīja*.

To the glorious, beginningless abode of the power of consciousness, *śikhā* (the crest-lock), *phaṭ*. To the glorious, independent abode of the power, *kavaca* (the armor), *vaṣaṭ*. To the glorious, eternally undecaying abode of the power, the three eyes, *netratraya*, *vauṣaṭ*. To the glorious, infinite abode of the power, the weapon (*astra*), *phaṭ*. [From] *tā* [up to] the end of the feet; thus ends the placement (*nyāsa*) of the Goddess of Speech (*Vāgdevatā*). Now follows the placement of the syllables of the Root-Mantra (*mūlavidyā*). One should place each individual syllable of the Root-Mantra in fifteen locations:
(3) *kaṃ* on the head; (3) *eṃ* in the secret place; (3) *īṃ* in the heart; (3) *laṃ* in the right eye; (3) *hrīṃ* in the left eye.

Having displayed the four mudrās— the Kṣobhiṇī and others, which are the weapons of the nine mudrās— one should meditate [on her] as she is anointed with saffron, her face kissed by an *āmalaka* fruit, her eyes possessing a gentle smile,

Having thus meditated and worshipped her mentally, then follows the placement (*nyāsa*) of the Mistress of the Wheel (*cakreśvarī*): (3) *aṃ āṃ sauḥ*, to the one presiding over the *Trailokyamohana-cakra* consisting of three squares.
Salutation to the Goddess Tripurā, who is of the form of the manifest Yoginīs accompanied by twenty-eight Śaktis;

[this is] at the thousand-petaled lotus below (3). Salutation to the sixteen Śaktis, beginning with Kāmākarṣiṇī, who preside over the Cakra consisting of the sixteen-petaled lotus that fulfills all desires, [beginning with] Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauḥ.

To the Goddess Tripureśī, who has the form of the Guhyayoginīs accompanied by their consorts, upon this petal named Viṣuva (the sixth); [and] to the eight Śaktis beginning with Anaṅgakusumā, who have the form of the most secret Yoginīs of the Sarvasaṃkṣobhaṇa-cakra consisting of an eight-petalled lotus, [beginning with] Hrīṃ Klīṃ Sauḥ... [to Tripura].

To the goddess Rasundarī, in the *ādhāra* (the foundational center): *haiṃ hsklīṃ hsauḥ*. To the form of the Yoginīs of the *sampradāya*, consisting of the fourteen spokes and bestowing all good fortune, beginning with Sarvasaṃkṣobhiṇī, to the goddess Tripuravāsinī, in the *svādhiṣṭhāna* (the self-sustaining center): *hsaiṃ hsklīṃ hsauḥ*.

In the *maṇipūra*, [resides] the venerable Tripurā, whose form is that of the Yoginīs who have transcended the *śākula* [state], consisting of the outer ten spokes, the accomplisher of all aims (*sarvārthasādhaka*), the bestower of all attainments (*sarvasiddhiprada*), and so forth; [and] within the inner ten spokes, [resides] the *nigarbha* [mantra] beginning with the omniscient one (*sarvajña*), consisting of the syllables *hrīṃ klīṃ bleṃ aṃ*.
In the Anāhata [cakra], to the goddess Tripuramālinī, who is the form of the Yoginīs, [I offer] *hrīṃ śrīṃ sauḥ*,

the essence of the eight [vowels], the remover of all diseases, and the eight secret Yoginīs beginning with Vaśinī; to the goddess Tripurāsiddhā, who is the form of the Yoginīs, in the Viśuddhi [cakra], [I offer] *hsraiṃ hsklīṃ hsrauḥ*, the essence of the triangle.

To the Goddess Tripurāmbā, who is the form of the most secret Yoginīs accompanied by the three powers beginning with Kāmeśvarī from the wheel that bestows all accomplishments (*sarvasiddhipradacakrā*), at the tip of the *laṃbikā* [the uvula], [I offer] the root-mantra consisting of the nature of *Brahman*,
which is composed of all bliss, along with the six limbs, weapons, and ten [powers], in the form of the supreme and non-supreme secret Yoginīs.
*Hā tripurasundaryai* (Obeisance to Tripurasundarī). In the *ājñā* [cakra]: again, at each one-finger-breadth interval above the *ājñā-cakra*, [one should place the mantras].
At the *bindu*: *aṃ āṃ sauḥ namaḥ*. At the half-moon (*ardhacandra*): *aiṃ klīṃ sauḥ*. At the *rodhinī*:
*hrīṃ klīṃ sauḥ*. At the *nāda*: *haiṃ hsklīṃ hsauḥ*. At the end of the *nāda* (*nādānta*): *hsaiṃ hasakalrīṃ hsraḥ*.

In Śakti: *hṛīṃ klīṃ bleṃ*. In Vyāpikā: *hṛīṃ śrīṃ sauḥ*. In Samānā: *hasraiṃ*. In Unmanā: the Root Mantra (*mūla*).
